zh.title: 加拿大航空波音 737 MAX 8 據報在棕櫚泉離場爬升時收到 TCAS 避讓指令
zh.summary: 航空媒體報導，加拿大航空 AC1769 航班11月17日自棕櫚泉起飛後，因附近一架塞斯納小飛機沒有回應，收到空中防撞系統（TCAS）爬升指令。班機續飛溫哥華平安降落，主管機關尚未公布調查結果。
body: 航空媒體 AeroSillage 與 Simple Flying 引述 AIRLIVE 報導，加拿大航空 AC1769 航班於11月17日自美國加州棕櫚泉國際機場（PSP）起飛，前往溫哥華國際機場（YVR）。飛機爬升至約11,400呎時，空中防撞系統（TCAS）發出避讓指令（Resolution Advisory），要求機組爬升至12,000呎。報導稱，當時附近一架塞斯納（Cessna）小飛機沒有回應。涉事飛機為波音 737 MAX 8，註冊號 C-FSDB。
班機沒有折返或轉降，續飛溫哥華後平安降落。AeroSillage 指出，Flightradar24 的航班紀錄可確認該機當天執飛棕櫚泉往溫哥華航線並抵達目的地，但完成飛行的紀錄本身無法證明 TCAS 是否發出指令，也無法顯示兩機的最近距離。
兩家媒體都指出，現有報導未說明塞斯納是未回應無線電呼叫，還是未依航管指示行動；該機的身分與兩機最小間隔也未公開。目前未見美國或加拿大主管機關就這起事件公布調查結果。

en.title: Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 reportedly received TCAS climb advisory after departing Palm Springs
en.summary: Aviation outlets report that Air Canada flight AC1769 received a TCAS resolution advisory to climb after departing Palm Springs on November 17, with a nearby Cessna said to be not responding. The flight continued to Vancouver and landed safely; no official findings have been published.
body: AeroSillage and Simple Flying, citing AIRLIVE, reported that Air Canada flight AC1769 departed Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) for Vancouver International Airport (YVR) on November 17. As the aircraft climbed through about 11,400 feet, its Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) issued a resolution advisory calling for a climb to 12,000 feet. A nearby Cessna was reportedly not responding. The aircraft was a Boeing 737 MAX 8 registered C-FSDB.

The flight did not return or divert and landed safely in Vancouver. AeroSillage said Flightradar24's flight record confirms the aircraft operated the Palm Springs–Vancouver service and reached its destination, but that a completed flight record cannot show whether TCAS issued a command or how close the two aircraft came.

Both outlets noted that the available reporting does not establish whether the Cessna failed to answer a radio call or did not comply with an air traffic control instruction. Its identity and the minimum separation have not been disclosed, and no findings from US or Canadian authorities on the encounter have been published.

facts.claim: AIRLIVE reported that AC1769, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 registered C-FSDB, received a TCAS resolution advisory to climb from about 11,400 feet to 12,000 feet after departing Palm Springs on November 17, with a Cessna not responding.
Flightradar24's record confirms the aircraft and route and its arrival in Vancouver, but not the TCAS command or separation.
No US or Canadian authority findings have established the circumstances; the Cessna's identity and minimum separation are undisclosed.
